title: Kīlauea Volcano — Overflight of Ocean Entry
place: Kapoho ocean entry, Kīlauea lower East Rift Zone, Hawaiʻi
notes: SPARE (sharp 1080p but less 'event'). Aerial view: huge white laze plume billowing from the shoreline (x~0.4-0.6,y~0.0-0.8), black lava delta, surf; dark tephra jets punch through the steam at the base. Source had a red annotation circle at ~7 s of the original; cut starts at 9 s, verified clean. Small USGS bug bottom-left. Best shot A 0-2.6, shot B 8-10.6.
fact_en: The interaction of molten lava flowing into cool seawater causes pulsating "littoral explosions" that throw spatter (fragments of molten lava) and pieces of solidified glassy lava (black sand, Pele's hair, limu o Pele) high into the air.
